sources.author: Harrison Chase
sources.headline: Co-founder & CEO @ LangChain
sources.post_summary: Discussed the rapid evolution of AI agents from simple chatbots to autonomous systems that can plan, execute, and iterate on complex tasks. Highlighted how LangGraph enables developers to build reliable agent workflows with state management and human-in-the-loop capabilities.

sources.author: Sarah Guo
sources.headline: Founder @ Conviction
sources.post_summary: Shared insights on the AI infrastructure layer becoming the new battleground, with companies racing to build the 'picks and shovels' for the AI gold rush. Covered GPU allocation challenges and the emergence of specialized inference platforms.

sources.author: Simon Willison
sources.headline: Independent AI Researcher
sources.post_summary: Demonstrated how LLMs can now write, debug, and deploy entire web applications autonomously using tools like Claude's computer use feature. Showed a live example of building a data visualization dashboard without writing code manually.

sources.author: Emmanuel Ameisen
sources.headline: Head of AI @ Anthropic
sources.post_summary: Explained the shift from prompt engineering to agent engineering, where developers now focus on designing agent architectures, tool integrations, and evaluation frameworks rather than crafting perfect prompts.

sources.author: Andrej Karpathy
sources.headline: AI Researcher & Educator
sources.post_summary: Posted about the emerging 'AI Software Engineer' role, where developers increasingly act as conductors orchestrating multiple AI agents rather than writing code directly. Discussed implications for software development workflows.

sources.author: Elena Rodriguez
sources.headline: GTM Engineer at OpenAI | Ex-Salesforce
sources.post_summary: Discusses how GTM engineering teams are moving beyond basic lead scoring to building predictive models that identify expansion opportunities within existing accounts. Shares a framework for mapping product usage data to revenue outcomes using custom attribution models.

sources.author: Marcus Chen
sources.headline: Head of Revenue Operations at Notion
sources.post_summary: Explains the shift from manual outbound processes to automated sequences that adapt based on prospect engagement signals. Details how his team reduced time-to-first-meeting by 40% while maintaining personalization at scale through dynamic content blocks.

sources.author: Sarah Kim
sources.headline: Content Strategy Lead at HubSpot | B2B SaaS
sources.post_summary: Shares data showing that content-led outbound campaigns outperform traditional cold outreach by 3x when content is mapped to specific buying committee roles. Outlines a content-to-pipeline attribution model that connects blog engagement to closed revenue.

sources.author: David Park
sources.headline: VP Sales Operations at Ramp
sources.post_summary: Details the operational infrastructure needed to scale outbound automation without creating technical debt. Covers the importance of building feedback loops between sales development and marketing teams to continuously optimize messaging based on response rates.

sources.author: Priya Sharma
sources.headline: Director of Revenue Operations at Figma
sources.post_summary: Examines how revenue operations teams can use intent data and buying signals to prioritize accounts for outbound campaigns. Shares a scoring methodology that combines firmographic data with behavioral signals to improve conversion rates by 60%.

sources.author: Arvid Kahl
sources.headline: Founder & Author | Bootstrapped to $1M ARR
sources.post_summary: Shared the exact revenue numbers and customer acquisition strategy for his latest micro-SaaS product after 90 days of building in public. Emphasized how transparent weekly updates helped him validate pricing and find early adopters through LinkedIn.

sources.author: Danny Postma
sources.headline: Solo Founder | AI Products | Ex-Meta
sources.post_summary: Documented the journey of pivoting from a failed AI wrapper idea to a successful niche tool for content creators. Detailed the technical decisions, failed experiments, and the moment he found product-market fit through user interviews.

sources.author: Sara Mauskopf
sources.headline: Founder & CEO at Winnie | YC Alum
sources.post_summary: Wrote about the decision to rebuild core features from scratch after user feedback revealed the original architecture couldn't scale. Shared the technical debt assessment process and how the team handled the 6-week rewrite without losing momentum.

sources.author: Paul Copplestone
sources.headline: CEO & Co-founder at Supabase
sources.post_summary: Posted about the early days of building Supabase as a solo technical founder, including the first 100 GitHub stars, initial user feedback loops, and the moment he decided to bring on a co-founder after hitting usage limits.

sources.author: Shaan Puri
sources.headline: Founder | Ex-CEO of Bebo | Investor
sources.post_summary: Shared his framework for evaluating side project ideas that actually have monetization potential. Broke down the difference between 'vanity projects' and 'painkiller products' using examples from his own failed and successful builds.
